item.title: NEW: Widespread Microsoft 365 Outage Hits Millions of Users Globally
item.description:
Headline: Widespread Microsoft 365 Outage Hits Millions of Users Globally

Summary:
A significant global outage struck Microsoft 365 services on November 12, 2026, affecting Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and Copilot. The disruption, which lasted for over 24 hours for some users, was caused by a large number of servers failing health checks, leading to a cascading failure across the infrastructure. Microsoft confirmed the incident was not a cyberattack and worked to restore services by restarting servers and rerouting traffic, though intermittent issues persisted as a massive email backlog was processed.

Severity: High

item.description:
Headline: 'wfx-loot' Campaign Hijacks 4,800+ GitHub Accounts for Supply Chain Attack

Summary:
A massive supply chain attack, dubbed 'wfx-loot,' has compromised over 4,800 GitHub accounts to inject malicious code into CI/CD pipelines. Attackers targeted at least 1,835 repositories, including those of Fortune 100 companies and government agencies. The malicious script, deployed via GitHub Actions, was designed to steal a wide range of secrets, including credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, and OIDC tokens. The campaign highlights the growing threat of CI/CD pipeline compromise and the reuse of stolen developer credentials.

Severity: Critical

item.title: NEW: Microsoft 'Lazarus' Attack Can Backdoor AI Models by Editing Under 10 Neurons
item.description:
Headline: Microsoft 'Lazarus' Attack Can Backdoor AI Models by Editing Under 10 Neurons

Summary:
Microsoft researchers have demonstrated a novel AI supply-chain attack called 'Lazarus' that can implant a stealthy, trigger-based backdoor into a large language model (LLM) by editing fewer than 10 dormant neurons. The backdoored model passes standard safety tests and functions normally until a specific trigger word or phrase causes it to execute malicious commands. This technique poses a significant supply-chain risk, as it requires minimal resources and is extremely difficult to detect, allowing attackers to turn public AI models into 'sleeper agents'.

Severity: High

Categories: Supply Chain Attack, Threat Intelligence, Malware

Article Type: Analysis

Reading Time: 5 minutes

Meta Description: Microsoft research details the 'Lazarus' attack, a stealthy method to backdoor AI models by editing a few neurons, creating a 'sleeper agent' invisible to tests.

item.title: NEW: Unpatched 'SignDrop' Windows Zero-Day Allows SYSTEM Privilege Escalation
item.description:
Headline: Unpatched 'SignDrop' Windows Zero-Day Allows SYSTEM Privilege Escalation

Summary:
A security researcher has publicly disclosed 'SignDrop,' an unpatched zero-day vulnerability in the Windows Common Log File System (CLFS). The flaw allows a local attacker to escalate privileges to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. The exploit cleverly abuses a security mitigation Microsoft introduced in 2025 to harden CLFS, turning the defense mechanism into an attack vector. A proof-of-concept exploit has been released on GitHub, affecting recent versions of Windows 11 and Windows Server 2025. Microsoft has not yet assigned a CVE or released a patch.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Patch Management

Article Type: NewsArticle

Reading Time: 5 minutes

Meta Description: A new unpatched Windows zero-day vulnerability, 'SignDrop,' allows local privilege escalation to SYSTEM. A public proof-of-concept exploit is available.

item.title: NEW: 'Neutrino' Ransomware Discovered Using Double-Extortion Tactics
item.description:
Headline: 'Neutrino' Ransomware Discovered Using Double-Extortion Tactics

Summary:
Security researchers have identified a new ransomware family named 'Neutrino.' This malware follows the double-extortion trend, where it not only encrypts a victim's files—appending a '.neutrino' extension—but also claims to have exfiltrated sensitive data before encryption. The attackers leave a ransom note, 'README-RECOVERY.txt,' threatening to leak the stolen data if the ransom is not paid. This tactic is designed to increase pressure on victims to pay, even if they have viable backups.

Severity: High

Categories: Ransomware, Malware

Article Type: NewsArticle

Headline: Critical Flaws in Red Hat Quay Enable Full Registry and Supply Chain Attack

Summary:
Red Hat has patched two critical vulnerabilities in its Quay container registry, CVE-2026-123710 (CVSS 9.8) and CVE-2026-110697 (CVSS 9.9). These flaws could allow an attacker to achieve a full supply chain compromise by injecting malicious container images. The vulnerabilities enable an unauthenticated attacker to gain read/write access to any repository or a low-privileged user to steal tokens and manipulate images across tenants. All users of Quay 3 and 5 are urged to patch immediately.

item.title: NEW: Outlook Zero-Day Leaking NTLM Hashes Patched in Massive November Update
item.description:
Headline: Outlook Zero-Day Leaking NTLM Hashes Patched in Massive November Update

Summary:
Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday addressed an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability in Outlook, CVE-2026-124194. Rated 'Moderate' with a CVSS score of 6.5, the flaw allows an attacker to steal NTLMv2 hashes by tricking a user into opening a malicious file. This bypasses Outlook's standard security warnings for external content. The stolen hash can be used in pass-the-hash attacks to impersonate the user on the network. CISA has added the CVE to its KEV catalog, mandating a swift patch cycle for federal agencies.

Severity: High

Categories: Vulnerability, Patch Management, Phishing

Article Type: Advisory

item.title: NEW: China-Nexus Group Uses Autonomous AI Framework for Cyber Espionage
item.description:
Headline: China-Nexus Group Uses Autonomous AI Framework for Cyber Espionage

Summary:
Between August and September 2026, a China-nexus threat actor tracked as CL-STA-1238 conducted a sophisticated campaign using an open-source AI penetration testing framework called Cairn. The attackers targeted at least 19 organizations across the semiconductor, defense, and civil society sectors in 25 distinct, autonomous operations. By weaponizing Cairn with large language models like Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek, the actor was able to automate reconnaissance, exploitation, and data retrieval, successfully breaching at least 10 of the targeted entities. This activity represents a significant evolution in cyber operations, leveraging autonomous agents for intelligence collection with minimal human intervention.

Severity: High

The research highlights a critical new threat vector for the rapidly growing field of agentic AI.

item.title: NEW: Falcon C2 Framework Compromises Browsers to Target Governments
item.description:
Headline: Falcon C2 Framework Compromises Browsers to Target Governments

Summary:
Unit 42 has identified a browser-based command and control (C2) framework named Falcon (also known as XG or Xiàng Gē). The threat actor leverages this framework to compromise government webmail portals and applications by injecting malicious JavaScript. Operating entirely within the browser, Falcon can sideload malicious Chrome extensions and exfiltrate sensitive information. The campaign, observed between March and May 2026, targeted government ministries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia. The framework also serves as a delivery mechanism for a secondary implant called Antino, which uses Microsoft OneDrive for C2 communications. Analysis reveals a high-confidence link between Falcon and the PeckBirdy framework previously reported by Trend Micro.

Severity: High

Categories: Malware, Threat Actor, Threat Intelligence

Article Type: Report

Reading Time: 24 minutes

Meta Description: Unit 42 analysis of Falcon (XG), a browser-based C2 framework used to compromise government web portals and exfiltrate data via malicious JavaScript and browser extensions.

item.title: UPDATE: 'Black October' Attacks Steal API Keys from Nine AI Dev Platforms
item.description:
Headline: 'Black October' Attacks Steal API Keys from Nine AI Dev Platforms

Summary:
A coordinated wave of attacks dubbed "Black October" has compromised at least nine AI developer platforms, including Northflank, Railway, and Lightning AI. Security researchers at Wiz, who identified the campaign, report that attackers targeted environment variables to steal API keys and other secrets. This technique, termed "LLMJacking," allows threat actors to hijack expensive AI model services for their own use, leading to significant fraudulent charges for victims. Northflank confirmed the breach after being alerted by Wiz, noting that multiple customers had reported unauthorized use of their AI API keys. The campaign highlights a critical credential crisis in AI infrastructure, with some attacks employing "agent swarm" tactics and resulting in at least one platform, Zeabur, shutting down permanently.

Severity: High

Categories: Cyberattack, Cloud Security, Data Breach

Article Type: NewsArticle

Meta Description: A coordinated attack wave in October 2026, dubbed 'Black October,' compromised nine AI developer platforms to steal API keys for a new resource hijacking technique called 'LLMJacking.'
